argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only on a qualified basis. Aggregate readiness and general launch checks support launch readiness, but the same record also shows that long-context onboarding support is a named deployment context with missing evaluation coverage. The overbroad point is any implication of clean, full-coverage certification. The narrower supportable position is that certification can be defended if the packet and model-card treatment are limited to completed evaluations and present the long-context onboarding gap as unknown rather than passed.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost claim is needed to justify the narrower position. The supportable governance path is to avoid escalation by treating the issue as a disclosure-and-scope condition rather than as evidence of failed aggregate readiness.
claims_about_policy: The policy text requires disclosure of material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts. It also distinguishes general readiness evidence from named-context coverage. On this record, policy does not support a clean no-limitation certification claim for long-context onboarding support. It does support a caveated certification posture tied to completed evaluations and explicit disclosure of the named-context gap.
concessions: The current admissible record does not support any claim of full evaluation coverage for long-context onboarding support.
The draft model-card statement described in the record is too strong if it treats missing evaluations as evidence of no limitation.
The present record does not prove that the final packet artifacts already contain the required disclosure language.
